title: The corrected semi-abelian Kummer input
statement: Let $k$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ and let $1\to T\to G\to A\to1$ be a semi-abelian variety over $k$. Then \[ \bigcap_{n\geq1}nG(k)=0, \qquad G(k)\longrightarrow H^1_{\rm cts}(G_k,TG) \quad\hbox{is injective}. \] Consequently, for an immersion $U\hookrightarrow G$, two $k$-points with the same abelianized section class are equal. The corresponding map on algebraic points and germs of sections is injective.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.1 and its following proof
limitations: The semi-abelian embedding hypothesis is retained; G(k) itself is not asserted finitely generated.

title: Excluded types and explicit failures over larger fields
statement: For $\mathbb P^1$ and $\mathbb A^1$ in characteristic zero the geometric fundamental group is trivial, so every rational point gives the same section. On the hyperbolic curve $U_0=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ over $\mathbb R$, the distinct points $2$ and $3$ give the same section class. For every prime $p$, put \[ k=\mathbb Q_p((t^{\mathbb Q})),\qquad x=2,\qquad y=2+t. \] This is a $p$-adically closed field which is not sub-$p$-adic, and $x,y$ give the same full arithmetic section class on $U_0/k$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.2 and its following proof
limitations: The Hahn field is explicitly not finitely generated over Qp and is not a counterexample to B(d) in that field class.

title: Uniformizers, tangent vectors, and Deligne's fibre functor
statement: Let $y\in X(k)$ and let $R$ be its henselian local ring, with fraction field $L$ and residue field $k$ of characteristic zero. A uniformizer $t$ defines a splitting of $G_L\to G_k$. Replacing $t$ by $t(1+h)$, $h\in\mathfrak m_R$, preserves its inertia-conjugacy class. The splitting classes form a torsor under $H^1(k,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1))=\widehat{k^\times}$. The classes defined by nonzero tangent vectors form the $k^\times$-Kummer orbit in this torsor and are precisely Deligne's tangential fibre functors.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.3 and its following proof
limitations: The tangent/uniformizer sign convention is fixed in the proof; the global intrinsic recognition problem belongs to F(g).

title: Ramification and the two differential maps
statement: At rational boundary points of a finite morphism of curves, choose parameters with $t=a u^d(1+h)$, $a\in k^\times$, $h\in(u)$. In tangent coordinates the induced map of packets is \[ \widehat{k^\times}\longrightarrow\widehat{k^\times}, \qquad c\longmapsto a c^d. \] It restricts to the homogeneous map of tangent vectors $v\mapsto a v^d$. In the pure local model $t=a u^d$, the trace and the determinant norm of differentials satisfy respectively \[ \operatorname{Tr}_{k((u))/k((t))}(du/u)=dt/t, \qquad \operatorname{Nm}(du)= (-1)^{d-1}d^{-d}a^{-1}t^{1-d}(dt)^{\otimes d}. \] The latter equality is in the norm of the one-dimensional differential space, identified with $(\Omega^1_{k((t))/k})^{\otimes d}$ by $dt$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.4 and its following proof
limitations: Trace of logarithmic forms and determinant norm of differentials are typed separately and both formulas are proved.

title: Abelianized fibres in positive genus
statement: Let $k/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated and let $g(X)\geq1$. Write $r=|S(\bar k)|$. In the map from rational points and full rational cuspidal packets to geometrically abelianized section classes: \begin{enumerate} \item every rational point has a singleton fibre; \item images belonging to different rational cusps are disjoint, and are disjoint from all rational point images; \item for $r=1$ the entire unique packet has one abelianized image; \item for $r\geq2$ the map on every packet is injective. \end{enumerate} For $r=0$ the domain consists only of the rational points.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.5 and its following proof
limitations: Finitely generated characteristic-zero base field; positive genus, including the entire one-cusp collapse.

title: Genus-zero abelian fibres, including the exceptional collisions
statement: Let $k/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, $g(X)=0$, and put $r=|S(\bar k)|$. An anisotropic conic has neither rational interior points nor rational cusps, so the domain in question is empty. Otherwise choose a rational interior point as $\infty$ and write $S\subset\mathbb A^1(\bar k)$. In the coordinate torsor for $H^1(k,\Delta_U^{\rm ab})$, the point and packet maps are represented by \[ v(x)_s=x-s,\qquad v(y,a)_s=\begin{cases}a&s=y,\\y-s&s\ne y,\end{cases} \quad a\in\widehat{k^\times},\ y\in S(k). \] Two such vectors represent the same class precisely when their quotient is the restriction of a single diagonal element of $\widehat{k^\times}$. For $r\geq4$ every nonempty fibre on this domain is a singleton. For $r=3$ the only nonsingleton fibres consist of one element in each of two distinct rational cusp packets. For three rational cusps $y,z,w$, their unique pairwise intersection is \[ a=\frac{y-w}{z-w}(z-y),\qquad b=\frac{y-z}{(y-w)/(z-w)}. \] The three pairwise intersections are distinct. For $r=2$ with split boundary, every abelian class has one element in each cusp packet and additionally one interior point exactly when the class is in $\kappa(k^\times)$. For $r\leq1$ the geometric group is trivial and all elements of the domain have the same image.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.6 and its following proof
limitations: Finitely generated characteristic-zero base field; counts only rational point/cusp domain. In an anisotropic conic that domain is empty.

printed_status: Proved using the prompt's local theorem
title: The complete neighbourhood deduction of (T1)
statement: For a finite extension $k/\mathbb Q_p$ and a hyperbolic $U/k$, the map \[ U(k)\ \sqcup\!\coprod_{y\in S(k)}\operatorname{Sect}(D_y/G_k)/I_y \longrightarrow \operatorname{Sect}(\Pi_U/G_k)/\Delta_U \] is bijective. Each packet is a torsor under $\widehat{k^\times}$. The external input used for surjectivity is precisely Theorem 1.1 of the attached October 6, 2026 preprint \cite{B_OpenAIPadic}; its unrefereed provenance is retained in the source audit.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.7 and its following proof
limitations: Uses the prompt-stipulated unrefereed local Theorem1.1. The complete affine reduction is supplied, but a complete independent referee verification of the input is not claimed.

title: The $p$-adic tangential subpacket and all its point limits
statement: For $k/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, a uniformizer $\varpi$ gives \[ k^\times=\varpi^{\mathbb Z}\times\mathcal O_k^\times, \qquad \widehat{k^\times}=\varpi^{\widehat{\mathbb Z}} \times\mathcal O_k^\times. \] The Kummer map is injective, has cokernel $\widehat{\mathbb Z}/\mathbb Z$, and has dense image. At a rational cusp, every packet element is a limit of point sections of points tending to that cusp in the $p$-adic topology. Every convergent limit of such point sections belongs to that packet.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.8 and its following proof
limitations: Local finite extension of Qp; this does not establish a global intrinsic tangential criterion.

title: Genus zero and genus one over a $p$-adic field
statement: For a smooth proper genus-zero curve over $k/\mathbb Q_p$ there is exactly one arithmetic section class, including for an anisotropic conic. For an elliptic curve $E/k$ with its origin, the section set is $H^1(k,TE)$ and there is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow E(k)\longrightarrow H^1(k,TE) \longrightarrow T H^1(k,E)\longrightarrow0. \] Local Tate duality identifies the last group with $\mathbb Z_p^{[k:\mathbb Q_p]}$ noncanonically. The point-section image is closed; its closure is exactly $E(k)$. For a genus-one torsor $C$ under $E$, the section set is empty exactly when its extension class $\delta([C])\in H^2(k,TE)$ is nonzero. This class vanishes exactly for the maximal divisible subgroup of $H^1(k,E)$. When it vanishes, the section set is a torsor under $H^1(k,TE)$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.9 and its following proof
limitations: Finite extension of Qp. The genus-one torsor class must lie in the maximal divisible subgroup; the classification is not a hyperbolic example.

title: Every full-section action has trivial fixed group
statement: Let $k$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$, or finite over $\mathbb Q_p$. For every section $s$ of a hyperbolic curve and every open subgroup $G'\subseteq G_k$, \[ C_{\Delta_U}(s(G'))=1. \] In particular this condition, appearing as axiom (3) and in scan 431, holds for point sections and for all cuspidal sections.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.10 and its following proof
limitations: Full Galois group and its open subgroups; the cyclotomic-kernel precision is supplied in Part F.

title: The exact classification of effective lifts
statement: For a centre-free profinite geometric group $\Delta$, a continuous outer action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Out}(\Delta)$ has the canonical extension \[ E_\rho=\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta) \times_{\operatorname{Out}(\Delta)}G. \] Its effective lifts are its splittings. After choosing one lift $\alpha$, their classes are exactly $H^1_{\rm cts}(G,\Delta_\alpha)$. An outer action arising from a hyperbolic affine curve with a rational cusp has effective lifts in that cusp packet. Every such lift normalizes the corresponding inertia group, including the non-tangential elements of the packet.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.11 and its following proof
limitations: Centre-free geometric kernel; intrinsic admissibility is not defined merely by choosing an arbitrary lift.

title: Vanishing fixed kernel proves uniqueness, not existence
statement: For a partial splitting over an open normal subgroup $H\triangleleft G$ of an extension $1\to L\to E\to G\to1$, the equality $L^H=1$ does not imply that the partial splitting extends. The exact additional condition is that $N_E(s(H))\to G$ be surjective. When it is surjective and $L^H=1$, its inverse is the unique extension.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.12 and its following proof
limitations: Refutes the prompt implication from L^H=1 alone. Scan421 itself already distinguishes normalizer-surjectivity existence from uniqueness; full geometric axiom6 is not refuted.

title: The geometric meanings of axioms (1)--(6)
statement: For actions arising from pointed curves over the fields in B.10, with admissible points defined as the actual interior point sections, axioms (1)--(4) of scans 412--415 hold. The three clauses (a)--(c) of axiom (5) are exactly exclusion of the deleted point, injectivity, and lifting of every other point. They hold in the geometric subcategory. Axiom (6) holds there by effective descent of the curve and its finite set of points, whenever the filled curve remains hyperbolic. The fixed subgroup of its actual forgetting kernel is trivial, including when the removed points are unordered. For intrinsic admissibility defined only by absence of a normalized cusp, axiom (5) is the additional point-surjectivity assertion, after the already proved point and packet injections.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.13 and its following proof
limitations: Geometric subcategory proved. The actual forgetting kernel has no fixed element, including unordered markings, provided both curves remain hyperbolic. General intrinsic axioms5-6 and the full requested implication diagram remain incomplete.

title: Finite support at finite places forces a point or a cusp
statement: Let $U/k$ be hyperbolic over a number field and let $s$ be a Selmer section. Let $Z\subset X$ be finite over $k$. Suppose the compactification point of $s_v$ belongs to $Z(k_v)$ for a set of finite places of density one. Then $s$ is induced by a point of $Z(k)\cap U(k)$ or is cuspidal at a point of $Z(k)\cap S(k)$. In particular, a section whose finite localizations are all cuspidal at one fixed rational cusp is globally cuspidal at that cusp.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.14 and its following proof
limitations: Requires Selmer localizations and density-one finite-place support in one finite subscheme; unrestricted global sections need not have support supplied by this argument.

printed_status: Proved using the prompt's local theorem
title: Affine modular cuspidality
statement: For $N$ with $g(X_1(N))\geq2$, every section of $\pi_1(Y_1(N))\to G_{\mathbb Q}$ is cuspidal on the affine curve. Its centre is the unique rational cusp determined on $X_1(N)$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.15 and its following proof
limitations: Uses prompt-stipulated local theorem and the verified proper modular conclusion; N has compact genus at least2.

title: Unrestricted section surjectivity for a constant family
statement: For $U_0=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ over a number field $k$ and a smooth geometrically connected base $S/k$ with a rational point, not every section of $\pi_1(U_0\times S)\to\pi_1(S)$ comes from a morphism $S\to U_0$. For geometric sections, deletion of a section retains precisely the sections disjoint from it at every geometric point of the base.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.16 and its following proof
limitations: Refutes unrestricted raw surjectivity. The exact geometric disjointness condition is proved, not a classification of all intrinsic admissible family sections.

title: A tautological complete section cannot lift through its deletion
statement: Let $g\geq2$, $n\geq1$, and $k$ have characteristic zero. For the universal curve over $\mathcal M_{g,n/k}$, none of the $n$ tautological complete sections admits a lift to a section of the fundamental-group extension after all $n$ markings are removed. This remains true after every finite \emph{\'etale} base change of degree $d$. The obstruction can be detected by a finite $\mu_m$-extension, for a prime $m\nmid d(2g-2)$, with $d=1$ on the original base.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.17 and its following proof
limitations: Genus≥2, at least one marking, and every finite étale base cover. The finite Chern obstruction applies to lifts of tautological complete classes; choose a prime coprime to the cover degree and 2g−2.

printed_status: Proved using the specified universal-curve input
title: No sections of the universal punctured family in genus at least three
statement: Over $k/\mathbb Q$ finitely generated, for $g\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, the universal punctured curve over $\mathcal M_{g,n/k}$ has no fundamental-group section. The external input is precisely the complete-family section classification in \cite[Main theorem]{B_LuoWatanabe}; its status and the inspected proof step are recorded in the source audit. The same conclusion holds on its geometrically connected full symplectic level-$m$ covers over fields containing $\mu_m$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.18 and its following proof
limitations: Uses the exact supplied unrefereed complete-family classification for g≥3,n≥1. Does not quantify over arbitrary finite étale moduli covers.

printed_status: Proved using the prompt's local theorem
title: Local interpretation of admissibility and the stack $\mathcal M_{1,1
statement: $} For a hyperbolic curve over a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, the sections which normalize no cusp inertia subgroup are exactly its point sections. The same local point-or-cusp description, with its full automorphism groupoids, holds for a hyperbolic DM curve, including $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and the $S_3$-quotient of the tripod.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.19 and its following proof
limitations: Local finite extension of Qp; complete groupoid retained. Number-field global surjectivity for these stacks remains unfinished.

title: The lattice stabilizer for the tripod
statement: For the tripod over a number field $k$ with a rational base point, fix an embedding into $\mathbb C$ and the resulting discrete topological lattice in the geometric fundamental group. Its stabilizer in $G_k$ is trivial when the chosen embedding of $k$ is nonreal, and is generated by its complex conjugation when that embedding is real. The oriented lattice has trivial stabilizer in both cases. Thus the canonical oriented discretization claimed in scans 489--490 already fails for the tripod.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.20 and its following proof
limitations: Elementary tripod proof. B.31 completes the general type using the precise archimedean intersection theorem.

title: What the $\overline{\mathbb Q
statement: $-algebraic entry supplies} The reading of cote 148, scan 43 as obtaining ``sections Gal$/\mathbb Q$'' has the following verified pointwise content. A finite-type $\overline{\mathbb Q}$-curve with an algebraic point has, after a finite field of definition, a point-induced section; its intrinsic datum without that field is a germ over open subgroups of $G_{\mathbb Q}$, modulo geometric conjugacy. This datum determines the point under the semi-abelian hypothesis of cote 143, scans 4--5. The stronger reading asserting a $\mathbb Q$-model for every such curve is false. For a hyperbolic curve $U/\overline{\mathbb Q}$, the constants condition in cote 143, scan 2 gives the exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(U) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_{\rm abs}(U) \xrightarrow{\;\theta\;}\Gamma_U\longrightarrow1, \qquad \theta(f)=(f^*|_{\overline{\mathbb Q}})^{-1}. \] Its image $\Gamma_U$ is open in $G_{\mathbb Q}$, and need not equal $G_{\mathbb Q}$. A finite field of definition gives a continuous partial splitting. Conversely a continuous splitting over $G_K$ gives an effective $K$-form of the curve, with its boundary; conjugating by $\operatorname{Aut}_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}(U)$ gives precisely isomorphic forms.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.21 and its following proof
limitations: The two doubtful fragments in the first-pass transcription remain unresolved as readings. Pointwise finite-field-definition germ assertion is proved; stronger universal Q-model reading is refuted.

title: Kummer structure, crossings, and finite covers in cote 143
statement: For a curve, a chosen lift of a boundary point gives an actual homomorphism $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)\to\Delta_U$; changing that lift conjugates the map. Arithmetic transport acts through the cyclotomic character and the permutation of boundary points. At a strict normal crossing with $r$ branches, the corresponding local group is $\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)^r$ with its branch labels; the actual map to the global geometric fundamental group must also be retained. It need not be injective. For a finite \emph{\'etale} cover defined by $H\subseteq\Pi_U$, the boundary lifts and inertias are \[ H\backslash\Pi_U/D_y, \qquad H\cap gI_yg^{-1}, \] with the local ramification indices giving multiplication on each one-dimensional Kummer lattice. Every section germ lifts after restriction to a sufficiently small open subgroup.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.22 and its following proof
limitations: At crossings, retain the actual local-to-global inertia map, which may have a kernel. No claim of a full intrinsic reconstruction of G_Q is made.

printed_status: Proved using the specified universal-curve input
title: The unpointed universal curve in genus at least three
statement: For $k/\mathbb Q$ finitely generated and $g\geq3$, the fundamental-group extension of the universal complete curve over $\mathcal M_{g/k}$ has no section. The same argument applies to its full symplectic level covers included in \cite[Remark on topologically ample families]{B_LuoWatanabe}.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.23 and its following proof
limitations: Uses supplied n=1 classification for genus≥3; stated compatible symplectic level versions only.

title: Explicit low-genus finite \emph{\'etale
statement: multisections} The proposed absence of all admissible section germs for universal families has the following geometric counterexamples. \begin{enumerate} \item Over $\mathcal M_{0,4}=\mathbb P^1_\lambda\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, the universal four-punctured line acquires the interior section $x=t$ after the degree-two \emph{\'etale} cover $\lambda=t^2$. \item Over $\mathcal M_{1,1}$, the nonzero $m$-torsion of the universal elliptic curve, for every $m\geq2$, is a finite \emph{\'etale} multisection of the curve with its origin deleted. \item Over $\mathcal M_2$, the six Weierstrass points are a degree-six finite \emph{\'etale} multisection of the universal complete curve. \end{enumerate}
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.24 and its following proof
limitations: Explicit examples prove existence and refute a uniform no-multisection claim. They do not classify all low-genus or all open-subgroup cases.

title: The necessary moduli tests and the exact tripod test
statement: An actual marked curve over a number field satisfies the distinctness tests of scans 487--488: in positive genus the sections of its marked points remain pairwise distinct after all holes are filled; in genus zero they remain distinct in every three-puncture comparison in which they are interior points. Its rational interior point sections normalize no boundary inertia. For ordered type $(0,4)$ the moduli point map and the tripod point map are literally the same map under \[ \mathcal M_{0,4}(k)=k\setminus\{0,1\},\qquad \mathcal M_{0,4}\simeq\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}, \] where the four markings are $(0,1,\infty,\lambda)$. The Isom-form reconstructs at most one marked curve from an outer action which is already realized by a marked curve; it supplies no point of this moduli curve for an arbitrary section.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.25 and its following proof
limitations: Necessary criteria and the exact M0,4/tripod identification; sufficiency over number fields and arbitrary outer-action realization remain unfinished.

title: The range of the Hom-form for constant families
statement: Let $S$ and $U$ be hyperbolic curves over a number field $k$. A section of the constant-family extension is a homomorphism $h:\Pi_S\to\Pi_U$ over $G_k$. Every such $h$ with open image is induced by a unique dominant morphism $S\to U$. The homomorphisms with $h(\Delta_S)=1$ are exactly $s\circ p_S$ for field sections $s:G_k\to\Pi_U$; among them, the morphism-induced classes are exactly the constant morphisms at $k$-points of $U$. The corresponding graphs are the actual family sections in these two ranges.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.26 and its following proof
limitations: The elementary open-image and geometrically trivial-image ranges. B.33 completes the image classification for constant families; general nonconstant families and the field-section term remain unfinished.

title: The unresolved part of Part B
statement: The following requested conclusions have not been proved or refuted here: point-surjectivity for all zero-cyclotomic-centralizer sections of the tripod over a number field; the same point-or-cusp dichotomy for every nonisotrivial hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated positive-transcendence-degree extension of $\mathbb Q_p$; all intrinsic instances of axioms (5)--(6) outside the geometric subcategory; section classification over arbitrary open subgroups of $\pi_1(\mathcal M_{g,n})$ and the remaining cases in genus at most two; the general intrinsic realization criterion for arbitrary admissible outer actions.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.27 and its following proof
limitations: Explicit incomplete ledger, updated after B.41 to retain the nonisotrivial p-adic case. B(g) is completed in B.31, stable-boundary exclusion in B.37, and the uniform tangential recognition in F.45; the narrower GT-automorphism-only formula remains in F.24.

title: The collision test for equation (25)
statement: The map of scan 409, equation (25), is injective for a smooth marked curve over a field finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. Its assertion for an arbitrary section of the arithmetic moduli extension, without the distinctness admissibility condition of scan 487, is false. Already for $\mathcal M_{0,5}$ two different marked holes can induce the same section after they are both filled.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.28 and its following proof
limitations: Refutes an unrestricted reading; geometric injectivity and the manuscript admissibility reservation are retained.

title: All fibres over the geometric locus of a deletion map
statement: Let $V/k$ be a hyperbolic curve over a number field, let $y\in V(k)$, and put $U=V\setminus\{y\}$. For the natural map \[ q_*:\operatorname{Sect}(\Pi_U/G_k)/\Delta_U \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sect}(\Pi_V/G_k)/\Delta_V, \] the fibre over $s_x$, $x\in V(k)\setminus\{y\}$, is the singleton $\{s_x\}$; the fibre over $s_y$ is the entire cusp packet at $y$. For every individual cuspidal class at a boundary point $z$ of $V$, its fibre is one class in the corresponding packet of $U$. Thus $q_*$ induces a bijection from the actual interior point classes of $U$ onto those of $V$ other than $s_y$ and induces an isomorphism on each old cusp packet. For every proper hyperbolic $X/k$ with $X(\mathbb A_k)_\bullet^{\mathrm{f\text{-}cov}}=X(k)$, all its hyperbolic open subcurves have only point and cuspidal sections.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.29 and its following proof
limitations: Computes all fibres over the geometric locus. Fibres over unknown nongeometric filled-curve sections are not classified.

printed_status: Proved using the prompt's local theorem
title: A configuration section above distinct point classes
statement: Let $U/k$ be hyperbolic over a number field and let $\operatorname{Conf}_n(U)\subset U^n$ be its ordered configuration space. Fix pairwise distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in U(k)$. The fibre of \[ \operatorname{Sect}(\pi_1(\operatorname{Conf}_n(U))/G_k) /\pi_1(\operatorname{Conf}_n(U)_{\bar k}) \longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Sect}(\Pi_U/G_k)/\Delta_U \] over $([s_{x_1}],\ldots,[s_{x_n}])$ is the singleton given by the actual configuration $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.30 and its following proof
limitations: Computes the fibre over an ordered tuple of distinct actual point classes. It does not force arbitrary coordinate section classes to be geometric.

title: The lattice stabilizer in every hyperbolic type
statement: Let $U/k$ be hyperbolic over a number field, $x\in U(k)$, and $\iota:k\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$. Every extension $j:\bar k\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ gives a dense discrete subgroup \[ \Lambda_j=\operatorname{im}\bigl( \pi_1^{\rm top}(U_\iota(\mathbb C),x_\iota) \longrightarrow\Delta_U\bigr) \] whose profinite completion is $\Delta_U$. Use $x$ for the effective action $\rho_x:G_k\to\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta_U)$, and let $\sigma\cdot j=j\circ\sigma^{-1}$. Then \[ \Lambda_{\sigma\cdot j}=\rho_x(\sigma)(\Lambda_j),\qquad \operatorname{Stab}_{G_k}(\Lambda_j)=G_{v,j}. \] Here $G_{v,j}=1$ at a complex place and is the order-two group of complex conjugation at a real place. The stabilizer of the oriented lattice is $1$. The unoriented orbit is $G_k/G_{v,j}$ and the oriented orbit is a free transitive $G_k$-set of these comparisons. Thus the effective action does not make the discretization independent of the embedding choice.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.31 and its following proof
limitations: Number field, actual rational base point, full profinite geometric group, with a specified complex embedding. The cited outer intersection theorem is converted to the actual based subgroup stabilizer.

title: All sections of proper constant families over a finite $p$-adic field
statement: Let $k$ be finite over $\mathbb Q_p$, let $S/k$ be a hyperbolic curve, and let $X/k$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two. Every continuous homomorphism $h:\Pi_S\to\Pi_X$ over $G_k$, modulo conjugation by $\Delta_X$, is induced by a unique $k$-morphism $S\to X$. Consequently the graph construction is a bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_k(S,X) \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Sec}\bigl(\pi_1(X\times_k S)\to\Pi_S\bigr), \tag{B.32.1} \] where section classes on the right are taken modulo the geometric fibre group $\Delta_X$. This closes the intermediate-image case of B.26 for this field and proper-fibre range.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.32 and its following proof
limitations: Finite extension of Qp, hyperbolic base curve and proper hyperbolic constant fibre. Uses the prompt-stipulated local theorem over every finite extension. General nonconstant families remain incomplete.

printed_status: Proved using the prompt's local theorem
title: The complete constant-family decomposition and its cusp parameters
statement: Let $k$ be a number field or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and let $S/k$ and $U=X\setminus D$ be hyperbolic curves. Write $\operatorname{Sec}^{\mathrm{nc}}(U/k)$ for the field section classes outside all cusp packets. For each $y\in D(k)$ choose its inertia and decomposition groups $I_y\subset D_y$ and put \[ \mathcal C_y(S)= \operatorname{Hom}_{G_k}(\Pi_S,D_y)/I_y. \] There is a disjoint decomposition, through the actual product and graph maps of (B.32.1), \[ \operatorname{Sec}\bigl(\pi_1(U\times_k S)\to\Pi_S\bigr) \simeq \operatorname{Hom}^{\mathrm{dom}}_k(S,U) \ \amalg\ \operatorname{Sec}^{\mathrm{nc}}(U/k) \ \amalg\ \coprod_{y\in D(k)}\mathcal C_y(S). \tag{B.33.1} \] Each $\mathcal C_y(S)$ is a torsor under $H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Pi_S,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1))$. The choice of a nonzero tangent at $y$ supplies its origin. If $k$ is a number field, there is the canonical Kummer identification \[ H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Pi_S,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1)) \simeq \varprojlim_n \mathcal O(S)^\times/ \mathcal O(S)^{\times n}. \tag{B.33.2} \] The right side is a power completion and is not asserted compact. Inflation from $G_k$ is exactly the subgroup arising from the constant units $k^\times$. Thus all intermediate geometric images in a constant family are accounted for by these cusp torsors. The remaining noncuspidal surjectivity question in (B.33.1) is precisely the field-section question already isolated in B.27.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.33 and its following proof
limitations: The decomposition is complete, retaining the exact noncuspidal field-section term. Its surjectivity from number-field points remains unresolved. The unit identification is proved for number fields, and means the displayed power completion.

title: The unrestricted interior-point reflection in the printed RNS Theorem F(ii)
statement: Let $k=\mathbb Q_5$, and let \[ Y=\mathbb P^1_k\setminus\{0,1,\infty,2\},\qquad Z=\mathbb P^1_k\setminus\{0,1,\infty\},\qquad f:Y\hookrightarrow Z. \] A tangential section $s$ at the cusp $2$ of $Y$ is not a point section of $Y$, whereas $f_*s$ is the point section of $2\in Z(k)$. This satisfies every field, prime, subgroup and map hypothesis in the literal interior-point statement of Mochizuki--Tsujimura, Theorem F(ii), and Proposition 3.5(iii) \cite{A_MochizukiTsujimuraRNS}. Thus the stated equivalence for arbitrary dominant morphisms, with point sets $Y(\Omega^H)$ and $Z(\Omega^H)$, is false. The same curves and sections over $\mathbb Q$ refute its unrestricted number-field analogue. This statement concerns that specific reflection assertion; it makes no assertion against the source's RNS Theorem A or its Isom theorems.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.34 and its following proof
limitations: Refutes precisely the printed interior-point reflection under arbitrary dominant morphisms, with every local hypothesis checked. No claim is made against RNS Theorem A or its Isom uses.

printed_status: Proved, using the stipulated local theorem
title: The exact fibre over a point under a dominant morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a number field or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and let $f:Y\to Z$ be a dominant morphism of hyperbolic curves over $k$. Write $\bar f:\bar Y\to\bar Z$ for its extension to smooth proper completions. For $z\in Z(k)$, the full-section fibre is the disjoint union \[ f_*^{-1}([s_z]) =\{[s_y]:y\in Y(k),\ f(y)=z\} \ \sqcup\! \coprod_{\substack{c\in(\bar Y\setminus Y)(k)\\ \bar f(c)=z}} \operatorname{Packet}_c(Y). \tag{B.35.1} \] In particular, dominant morphisms preserve point geometricity, and they reflect it on noncuspidal source sections. Finite morphisms preserve and reflect point geometricity on all sections. For finite \emph{\'etale} morphisms the latter assertion follows directly from the finite-cover action on the fibre over $z$, without the stipulated local theorem and over every characteristic-zero field.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.35 and its following proof
limitations: Computes the entire fibre over an actual point of the target, using the stipulated local theorem and finite-support descent. The finite-etale special case is independent of that theorem. Fibres over unknown nongeometric target classes remain uncomputed.

title: A closed obstruction to smooth arithmetic realization
statement: Fix a hyperbolic type $(g,n)$, its geometric full profinite curve group $\Delta$, and its prescribed peripheral conjugacy classes. Let $Q\subset\operatorname{Out}(\Delta)$ be the closure of the geometric mapping class group, and let $A\subset\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)$ be its inverse image. For each nonempty stable multicurve type, choose oriented generators $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\Delta$ of its node groups. Call their $A$-translates, with arbitrary individual conjugations, \emph{pro-simple multicurve tuples}. Let $k$ be a number field, let $E\twoheadrightarrow G_k$ be a profinite extension, and let $\rho:E\to\operatorname{Out}(\Delta)$ be continuous, with the image of the geometric kernel contained in $Q$. The following condition on a continuous section $s$ defines a closed, geometric-conjugacy-invariant subset of its section space: there is a nonempty pro-simple multicurve tuple such that, for every $\gamma\in G_k$, there are a permutation $\sigma$ and signs $\epsilon_i\in\{1,-1\}$ satisfying \[ \rho(s(\gamma))(c_i) \ \sim_\Delta\quad c_{\sigma(i)}^{\epsilon_i\chi(\gamma)} \qquad(1\leq i\leq r). \tag{B.36.1} \] Here the left side is a conjugacy class, so the condition is independent of the representative of the outer automorphism. No outer action satisfying this condition is the peripheral outer action of a smooth marked curve over $k$, or over any finite extension of $k$ after restriction.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.36 and its following proof
limitations: A proved closed necessary obstruction over number fields, including all finite-extension germs. The compact orbits contain pro-simple tuples, not necessarily discrete simple curves. Absence of the obstruction is not asserted sufficient.

title: Stable-boundary cuspidal sections are non-admissible
statement: Let $k$ be a number field, $2g-2+n>0$, and set $\mathcal M=\mathcal M_{g,n,k}$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n,k}$. For a $k$-rational stable boundary object $x$, let $\mathcal V_x$ be the intersection with $\mathcal M$ of the henselian neighbourhood of its residual gerbe in $\overline{\mathcal M}$. Define \[ C_{\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}} =\bigcup_{x\in(\overline{\mathcal M}\setminus\mathcal M)(k)} \operatorname{Im}\bigl( \operatorname{Sec}(\mathcal V_x/k) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}(\mathcal M/k)\bigr), \qquad C^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}} =\overline{C_{\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}}}. \tag{B.37.1} \] Isomorphic boundary objects give the same term. For schemes this is the nearby-point definition of Carlson--Corwin; for stacks the residual gerbe and its finite automorphisms are retained as described below. Every section in $C^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\mathcal M,\overline{\mathcal M}}$ has an outer action on the universal geometric punctured curve group which is not realized by a smooth marked curve, even after restriction to any finite extension of $k$. In particular, these sections are non-admissible in the constructive sense of scans 480 and 487--488, and none is the section of an interior moduli point. The same conclusion holds for unordered markings, with the associated finite permutation quotient retained.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.37 and its following proof
limitations: Covers the closure of every packet relative to the canonical stable boundary, including stack stabilizers and unordered markings, over number fields. Carlson–Corwin compactification independence is used in its scheme scope; no arbitrary-stack compactification theorem is imported. Does not establish surjectivity outside the closed boundary set and does not use the stipulated local p-adic theorem.

printed_status: Proved using the stipulated local theorem
title: Unramification over a p-adic base curve
statement: Let $k/\mathbb Q_p$ be finite, let $B/k$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve, put $K=k(B)$, and let $f:X\to B$ be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected curves of genus at least two. Write $E_X=\pi_1(X)$, $E_B=\pi_1(B)$, and let $\Delta$ be the geometric generic fibre group. The actual generic-fibre comparison is \[ \pi_1(X_K)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ E_X\times_{E_B}G_K. \tag{B.38.1} \] Pullback along $G_K\twoheadrightarrow E_B$ induces a bijection \[ \operatorname{Sec}(E_X\to E_B) \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Sec}(\pi_1(X_K)\to G_K), \tag{B.38.2} \] where both sides are taken modulo conjugation by the same group $\Delta$. Every section on the left is point-theoretic over $k$: for each finite extension $l/k$ and each $b\in B(l)$, its restriction to the point section at $b$ is induced by a unique point of $X_b(l)$. The maps on algebraic sections and on fundamental-group sections fit in the commutative diagram \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \operatorname{Sect}_B(X)&\xrightarrow{\sim}&X_K(K)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \operatorname{Sec}(E_X\to E_B)&\xrightarrow{\sim}& \operatorname{Sec}(\pi_1(X_K)\to G_K). \end{array} \tag{B.38.3} \] The upper bijection is extension by properness. This statement does not assert surjectivity of either vertical map for a nonconstant family.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.38 and its following proof
limitations: Proves generic-section unramification and the exact bijection with relative fundamental-group sections over a smooth p-adic base curve. Every relative section is point-theoretic on all finite-extension fibres. Realization by a section of a nonconstant family remains unproved; the dominant Hom theorem is not applied outside its open range.

title: Geometric-image trichotomy over every sub-p-adic field
statement: Let $K$ be a sub-$p$-adic field, let $V/K$ be a smooth geometrically connected variety, let $U/K$ be a hyperbolic curve, and let $h:\pi_1(V)\to\pi_1(U)$ be a continuous $G_K$-homomorphism. Write $P_V,P_U$ for the geometric groups. Exactly one of the following holds: \[ h(P_V)\text{ is open in }P_U;\qquad h(P_V)=1;\qquad 1\ne h(P_V)\subset I_c \text{ for a unique lifted cusp }c. \tag{B.39.1} \] In the third case $h(\pi_1(V))\subset D_c$, and the underlying cusp is $K$-rational. In the second case $h$ factors through an actual section $G_K\to\pi_1(U)$; no point realization of that section is asserted. The transfer used here preserves the full geometric homomorphism. More precisely, there exist an extension $K\hookrightarrow F$, a countable field $F_0\subset F$, an embedding $F_0\hookrightarrow l$ into a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and a descended datum $(V_0,U_0,h_0)/F_0$ whose base change to $F$ is $(V_F,U_F,h_F)$. The base change to $l$ has the same geometric homomorphism through the characteristic-zero base-change isomorphisms, including the peripheral subgroups of the target. These are the actual field maps used; an embedding of $F$ into $l$ is unnecessary.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.39 and its following proof
limitations: Extends the open/trivial/cuspal geometric-image trichotomy to every sub-p-adic field by one coherent countable descent and a relation-preserving local-field embedding. The geometrically trivial case retains the exact field-section term; it is not asserted geometric.

title: Unramification over every smooth p-adic model
statement: Let $k/\mathbb Q_p$ be finite, let $S/k$ be a smooth geometrically connected variety, put $K=k(S)$, and let $X\to S$ be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected curves of genus at least two. With $\Delta=\pi_1(X_{\overline K})$, the actual generic-fibre comparison and restriction map are \[ \pi_1(X_K)\simeq \pi_1(X)\times_{\pi_1(S)}G_K, \qquad \operatorname{Sec}(\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(S)) \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Sec}(\pi_1(X_K)\to G_K). \tag{B.40.1} \] Both section sets use conjugation by $\Delta$. Every relative section on the left restricts at each $s\in S(l)$, for every finite $l/k$, to the section of a unique point in $X_s(l)$. The statement makes no assertion that every such relative section is induced by a morphism $S\to X$.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.40 and its following proof
limitations: All dimensions of a smooth finite-type p-adic model. The residue-field map to the base fundamental group need not be injective; the actual fibre product is retained. Generic realization for nonconstant families remains open.

title: The complete isotrivial p-adic function-field case
statement: Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\mathbb Q_p$, and let $U/K$ be a hyperbolic curve which becomes constant after a finite extension: there exist $K'/K$ finite, a finite $p$-adic field $k'\subset K'$, a hyperbolic curve $U_0/k'$, and an isomorphism \[ U_{K'}\simeq U_0\times_{k'}K'. \tag{B.41.1} \] For affine $U$ this hypothesis concerns the whole open curve, including its boundary. Let $\overline U$ be its smooth compactification and $D=\overline U\setminus U$. Then the natural map \[ U(K)\ \sqcup\!\coprod_{c\in D(K)} \operatorname{Sec}(D_c/G_K)/I_c \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Sec}(\pi_1(U)\to G_K) \tag{B.41.2} \] is bijective. Each packet is the usual torsor under $H^1(K,\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1))= \varprojlim_n K^\times/K^{\times n}$. In particular every proper isotrivial hyperbolic curve over such a field satisfies point-section surjectivity in every transcendence degree.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.41 and its following proof
limitations: Complete point-or-cusp classification for isotrivial hyperbolic curves over finitely generated Qp fields in every transcendence degree. In the affine case the entire marked open curve must become constant. General nonisotrivial curves are not included.

title: A compatible tower invisible on all closed fibres
statement: Let $k$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, choose $q\in k$ with $0<|q|<1$, and let $E_q/k$ be the Tate elliptic curve. Put $B=E_q\setminus\{O\}$. For every integer $n>1$ there is a geometrically connected finite \'etale cyclic cover \[ f_n:C_n\longrightarrow B,\qquad \deg(f_n)=n, \tag{B.42.1} \] whose fibre over every closed point $b\in B$ is the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k(b)$. Nevertheless, its generic fibre has no $k(B)$-point, and $f_n$ has no section over any nonempty open of $B$. The covers are compatible under divisibility and determine a continuous surjection \[ \omega:\pi_1(B)\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z} \tag{B.42.2} \] which is surjective on $\pi_1(B_{\bar k})$ and vanishes on every closed-point decomposition group. Thus the map \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}} (\pi_1(B),\widehat{\mathbb Z}) \longrightarrow \prod_{b\in B^{\mathrm{cl}}} \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}} (G_{k(b)},\widehat{\mathbb Z}) \tag{B.42.3} \] has a nonzero kernel.
proof_location: sections/B.tex, statement B.42 and its following proof
limitations: A completely split compatible Tate-curve tower gives a nonzero global quotient invisible on every closed-point decomposition group. This refutes the exact finite-cover local-point hypothesis needed by the inspected function-field transfer, but does not construct a nongeometric section of a proper hyperbolic family.
